plan.proposition: Each distinct LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE value in permit_limits.csv encodes a specific monitoring frequency obligation (samples or measurements per calendar period, or a non-periodic monitoring mode) that can be read directly from workspace permit-package text or an in-workspace code legend.

Permit Part I monitoring tables that state a MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY in plain language for the same permit number and pollutant/parameter as a structured permit_limits.csv row, allowing audited pairing of code to frequency
Narrative statement-of-basis or fact-sheet sections that state monitoring frequencies for the same facility parameters represented in structured limits
Permit language defining non-calendar modes (e.g., continuous monitoring, conditional retest reporting) for rows carrying sentinel-looking codes such as 99/99 or 09/99

packet.exact_semantic_question: What monitoring frequencies do opaque LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE values (e.g. 05/WK, 01/07, 01/01) establish?
packet.relation_contract: frequency codes must be interpreted for monitoring obligations

candidate_interpretations.statement: For calendar codes, LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE has the form NN/PP where NN is the number of required analyses and PP is a period token (01=day, 07=week, 30=month, 90=quarter, WK=week count literal), as inferred from permit-text frequency paired to the same permit and parameter.

codes_supported_in_workspace.05/WK: five analyses per week (permit text: 'Five/Week' or '5/Week')
codes_supported_in_workspace.01/01: one analysis per day (permit text: '1/Day' or 'Daily')
codes_supported_in_workspace.01/90: one analysis per quarter (permit text: '1/Quarter' or 'Once/Quarter')

candidate_interpretations.evidence_basis: Permit Part I tables name MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY in plain language for the same EXTERNAL_PERMIT_NMBR and PARAMETER_CODE as structured rows; no workspace file states the NN/PP rule explicitly.

candidate_interpretations.statement: 99/99 denotes continuous monitoring (not a periodic sample count), as used for NM0020583 flow with sample type Totalizing Meter.
candidate_interpretations.evidence_basis: Permit text says 'Continuous' for flow; structured row carries 99/99. Literal code string absent from documents.

candidate_interpretations.statement: 09/99 denotes conditional WET retest reporting triggered by test failure ('If required'), not a fixed calendar sampling frequency.

codes_supported_in_workspace.09/99: report only when retest required after WET failure

candidate_interpretations.evidence_basis: Permit retest table labels rows '(If required) Retest N'; structured WET retest parameters carry 09/99. Literal code string absent from documents.

candidate_interpretations.statement: Codes cannot be interpreted from workspace sources alone because no in-workspace codebook defines LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE and permit documents never print the opaque tokens.
candidate_interpretations.evidence_basis: PASS_TASK constraint; grep of documents/ finds zero literal code matches.

known_limitations: No workspace file defines LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE as a field or prints the opaque code strings; interpretation relies on permit-parameter crosswalk, which PASS_TASK cautions is not itself a code legend.
Sentinel codes 99/99 and 09/99 never appear in document text; their meanings are inferred only from row pairing with 'Continuous' and 'If required' retest language.
The general NN/PP encoding convention is not stated authoritatively anywhere in the workspace.
Coverage is limited to three permits (NM0000116, NM0020583, NM0028762); codes are only exemplified for parameters present in this dataset.
Conditional footnotes (e.g., aztec '*1 When discharging') modulate when monitoring applies but are separate from the code-to-frequency mapping.

judgment.grounding: Retained workspace snippets establish plain-language MEASUREMENT FREQUENCY obligations for named parameters on permits NM0020583, NM0000116, and NM0028762 (e.g., documents/farmington/final_permit.txt lines 56–86: pH Five/Week, TRC Daily, TDS 1/Week; documents/gcc/final_permit.txt lines 57–74: pH and Flow 1/Day, TSS 1/Week; documents/aztec/final_permit.txt lines 72–82: Flow 2/Week, TRC 1/Day, TDS 1/Quarter). sources/permit_limits.csv confirms eight distinct LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE values with no definition column. No retained snippet prints any opaque code token (05/WK, 01/07, 01/01, 99/99, 09/99, etc.) or states an NN/PP encoding rule. Candidate code meanings in the packet are tied to permit+parameter crosswalk between CSV rows and permit tables, which the packet itself flags as insufficient to serve as a code legend.
judgment.remaining_uncertainty: Whether LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE values encode count-over-period (NN/PP), whether sentinel codes 99/99 and 09/99 mean continuous monitoring and conditional WET retest respectively, whether the crosswalk generalizes beyond the three exemplified permits and eight observed values, and how to reconcile contradictory flow-frequency wording (Continuous + 99/99 in final permit vs five-times-per-week narrative in documents/farmington/statement_of_basis.txt line 642).

proposal.exact_grounding: Permit Part I plain-language frequencies (documents/farmington/final_permit.txt, documents/gcc/final_permit.txt, documents/aztec/final_permit.txt) paired structurally to CSV LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE values on matching EXTERNAL_PERMIT_NMBR and PARAMETER_CODE; narrative corroboration in documents/farmington/statement_of_basis.txt and documents/gcc/fact_sheet.txt. No workspace source states the NN/PP rule or prints code strings.
proposal.semantic_delta: Would map each LIMIT_FREQ_OF_ANALYSIS_CODE to a structured monitoring frequency (analysis count and calendar period, or sentinel semantics for 99/99 continuous and 09/99 conditional retest) on monitoring_requirement_fy2025.limit_freq_of_analysis_code, satisfying purpose B require_interpreted for monitoring_frequency_code.
proposal.remaining_uncertainty: General NN/PP convention is not authoritatively stated; sentinel codes lack document literals; crosswalk is structural not definitional; flow-frequency contradiction for NM0020583; coverage limited to three permits and eight code values observed in sources/permit_limits.csv.

refinement.why_necessary: Retrieved permit text establishes plain-language calendar sampling frequencies (1/Day, 1/Week, 5/Week, 2/Week, 1/Quarter, 2/month) that pair consistently with six of eight code values, but two codes (99/99, 09/99) attach to qualitatively different monitoring modes—continuous totalizing flow and conditional WET retest reporting—whose permit language never uses the opaque code strings and is not reducible to a samples-per-period calendar obligation.
